terra.problem: Saying the song is coming from everywhere at once adds timing and presents the call to praise as an event already happening.
The verse calls for the people of Sela to cry out from the mountaintops; it does not tell them to go up there.
Calling Sela a city in Edom relies on a fact outside the passage without giving its reference, 2 Kings 14:7.
Saying the people are sent up high adds an instruction to travel that the verse does not give.
Saying the water goes away right after God lays waste the mountains and hills adds a sequence of events the text does not specify.
The reference to Papa knowing about sitting in the dark draws on his backstory without identifying the drawer.
The claim that idols cannot answer is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not say that joy is for the ones God leads, or identify where the idol worshipers end up.
Saying the surprise is meant to be a surprise assigns an intention the text does not state.
The verse says their ears are open, not that their ears work fine.
Calling it a question for anyone listening specifies a broad audience where the text says only 'among you.'
The passage asks who will listen and obey; it does not call anyone to stay.
The passage does not identify the speaker as the people themselves.
